guides.title: Guides
guides.subtitle: Short how-tos for every part of the platform

board.title: Work on the board
board.summary: Columns, drag and drop, new tasks.
board.keywords: kanban column status drag move create wip limit swimlane
steps: Open Tasks. Each column is a status: To Do, In Progress, In Review, Completed.
Press N, or use “New task”, to add a task to the focused column.
Drag a card to another column to change its status — or pick it up with Space and move it with the arrow keys.
Open a project's own board from Projects to see only its tasks.
A column with a WIP limit warns you when it holds more tasks than the limit.

details.title: Everything inside a task
details.keywords: assignee label due date priority checklist subtask comment attachment custom field time
steps: Click a card to open it. Set the priority, due date, assignees and labels at the top.
Break the work down with a checklist or with subtasks; progress follows the ticked items.
Discuss in comments and attach files; mention a colleague with @ to notify them.
Custom fields, time tracking and linked GitHub items appear in the same window when they are switched on.

find.title: Find tasks fast
find.keywords: search filter saved view sort custom field list calendar
steps: Press / on the board or type in the search box to find a task by title or key (for example LK-12).
Filter by project, person, priority, label, due date or a custom field.
Save a filter combination as a view and open it again with one click.
Switch between board, list and calendar with the view switch above the tasks.

trash.title: Deleted tasks and restoring
steps: A deleted task goes to the Trash, not into thin air.
Open Tasks → Trash, find the task and press Restore; it returns to its project.
Subtasks that were deleted with their parent come back with it. If the parent is still in the Trash, restore the parent first.
Deleting and restoring need the “Delete tasks” permission.

channels.title: Channels and direct messages
channels.keywords: channel direct message dm private public create member
steps: Open Chat. The list in the left column holds your channels and direct messages.
Create a channel with the plus button; make it private to invite only chosen people.
Start a direct message by choosing a colleague from the people list.
Your status (online, away, do not disturb) is shown next to your name for everyone.

threads.title: Threads, mentions and saved messages
threads.keywords: thread reply mention pin saved reaction emoji notification
steps: Reply in a thread to keep a long discussion out of the main stream.
Mention a person with @ so they get a notification; @channel notifies everyone and needs a permission.
Pin an important message to the top of the channel, or save it for yourself.
React with an emoji instead of writing “ok”.

write.title: Write in the editor
write.keywords: editor slash markdown heading list table code format bold
steps: Open Docs and create a page in a space; the page tree is in the left column.
Type / to insert a heading, list, table, code block or quote.
Markdown works as you type: “# ” makes a heading, “- ” a list, “[] ” a to-do.
Press ? for the full list of shortcuts. Changes are saved automatically.

organise.title: Organise and share
organise.summary: Spaces, the page tree and the Trash.
organise.keywords: space tree move trash restore export markdown html
steps: Group pages into spaces and drag them in the tree to reorder or nest them.
Deleted pages go to Docs → Trash and can be restored.
Export a page as Markdown or HTML from its menu to use it elsewhere.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.summary: Connect the tools you already use.

calendar.title: Google Calendar and meeting reminders
calendar.summary: See your next meeting and join in one click.
calendar.keywords: google calendar meeting reminder join connect
steps: Open Integrations and connect Google Calendar with your Google account.
Your upcoming meetings appear in Calendar and in the sidebar with a Join button.
Choose how long before a meeting the reminder appears; disconnect at any time and the stored meetings are removed.

github.title: GitHub
github.summary: Link pull requests and issues to tasks.
github.keywords: github pull request issue branch link rule
steps: An administrator connects GitHub in Integrations.
Mention a task key (for example LK-12) in a pull request or commit to link it to the task.
Rules can move a task on its own, for example to In Review when a pull request is opened.

roles.title: Roles and security
roles.summary: Who can do what, and how to stay safe.

permissions.title: Roles and permissions
permissions.keywords: role permission owner admin member viewer custom access
steps: Every person has a role: Owner, Administrator, Member or Viewer.
Open Settings → Roles & permissions to see exactly what each role may do.
Create a custom role with a hand-picked set of permissions and give it to people in Settings → Members.
Permissions such as exporting data or seeing team performance can be given to any role.

security.title: Two-factor sign-in and sessions
security.keywords: 2fa two-factor authenticator totp recovery code password session device security
steps: Open your profile → Security and choose “Turn on two-factor sign-in”.
Scan the QR code with an authenticator app and enter the six-digit code.
Save the recovery codes somewhere safe: each one works once if you lose the phone.
An administrator can require two-factor sign-in for everyone in Settings → Access.

notifications.title: Choose your notifications
notifications.keywords: notification mention reminder email sound mute
steps: Open your profile → Notifications.
Switch off the kinds you do not need, for example meeting reminders; everything else stays on.
Sounds and chat mute settings are in the same profile area and in each channel's menu.

export.title: Import and export
export.summary: Take your data with you, or bring it in.

tasks.title: Tasks as a spreadsheet (CSV)
tasks.keywords: csv export import excel spreadsheet download upload
steps: Open Settings → Data & export and choose a project, or all projects, to download a CSV that opens in Excel, Numbers and Google Sheets.
To import, pick the project, choose a CSV file and press “Check the file”: nothing is created yet, and problem lines are listed.
Press Import to create the tasks. Columns: Title (required), Description, Status, Priority, Due date, Assignees, Labels.
The file you export can be imported again as it is.

docs.title: Documents and the team report
docs.summary: Markdown, HTML and the Performance CSV.
steps: Export any document page as Markdown or HTML from its menu.
The Performance page has its own “Download CSV” that follows the filters you picked.
Exporting needs the “Export data” permission, which administrators have by default.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.subtitle: Press ? on any page to see its own list

whatsNew.subtitle: Releases, what is coming and exactly what runs

changes.title: Task templates and recurring tasks
changes.text: Save a task as a template with its checklist, subtasks and due offset, create tasks from it in one step, and let daily, weekly or monthly tasks create themselves on a schedule.
tech: migration 00037 (task_templates, recurring_tasks); schedules are checked every minute

changes.title: Resetting a lost password without email
changes.text: Until email is set up, the person who runs the server can give an existing account a new one-time password and lift a sign-in lock with one command.
tech: adduser -reset <email>… (prints a one-time password, clears failed_login_count and locked_until, revokes refresh tokens)

changes.title: Smoother invitations
changes.text: A new person follows the link, sees their address already filled in and only chooses a password; someone who already has an account is told so and can reset the password. An invitee is never offered a workspace of their own.
tech: the app remembers an opened, unaccepted invitation and returns to it

changes.title: Welcome guide
changes.text: An animated setup for new accounts (name the workspace, who you are, photo, contacts, invite the team) and a shorter one for people who join by invitation. Each step saves as you go; Help → Quick start runs it again. WhatsApp is a new profile field.
tech: users.whatsapp, users.onboarded_at · migration 00036 (existing accounts count as set up)

changes.title: Help center
changes.text: Search across guides, a quick start, shortcuts, a status card and contact with the team, in English and Ukrainian.
tech: no API changes (support requests: see below)

changes.title: Time tracking redesigned
changes.text: One flow: timer and estimate on the task, a header menu with recent tasks, and a weekly timesheet on the Time page.

changes.title: New sign-in and registration
changes.text: A live product preview next to the form; registration asks for the password twice.

changes.title: Support requests
changes.text: Write to the workspace administrators from Help: a problem, an idea or a question, with a screenshot. Administrators get an email and an inbox with statuses.
tech: screenshots: PNG/JPEG/WebP ≤ 2 MB, checked by their first bytes

changes.title: Performance page
changes.text: Throughput, cycle and lead time, overdue share, work in progress, burn-up, cumulative flow and workload.

changes.title: Import tasks from CSV
changes.text: Check the file first, then import; the exported file imports back unchanged.

changes.title: Trash for tasks
changes.text: Deleted tasks wait in the Trash and are restored with their subtasks.

changes.title: Shortcut help and interface density
changes.text: Press ? on any page; choose a compact or comfortable density.
tech: one shortcut catalogue feeds the dialog, the board, the editor and Help

changes.title: Two-factor sign-in
changes.text: Authenticator app with one-time recovery codes; administrators can require it.

changes.title: Notification preferences
changes.text: Switch off the kinds of notifications you do not need.

changes.title: Filter and sort by custom field
changes.text: Narrow or order tasks by a custom field's value.

changes.title: Export tasks as CSV
changes.text: One row per task, for a project or the whole workspace.

changes.title: Column names follow the interface language
changes.text: Default columns no longer show names in the language the board was created in.
tech: display-time translation, renamed columns keep their name
